motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council request the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power to prepare an After Action Report on the Granada Hills and Porter Ranch water service disruption, including: • Cause of the Failure - A clear explanation of why the trunk line valve failed and any contributing factors. • Impact on the Community - A summary of how many people were affected, how long they were without service, and the effect on residents, businesses, and schools. • Prevention Strategies - Recommendations for preventing similar problems in the future. • Temporary Service Measures - A review of the emergency and innovative steps taken to provide residents with water during the outage. • Communication Efforts — An evaluation of how information was shared with the public throughout the incident. I FURTHER MOVE that LADWP present this report to the City Council within 90 days of the adoption of this motion, and that the report be made available to the public. PRESENTED BY AA2________ JOHN S. LEE Councilmember, 12th District SECONDED BY AUG 1 2 2025

documents.excerpt: Council File No. 25-0922 Granada Hills / Porter Ranch Water Service Disruption After Action Report August 18, 2026 INCIDENT DETAILS • August 5,2025- Incident Occurred • 24-Inch Horizontal Gate Valve Failed in the Closed Position • 9,200 Service Connections Affected (~31,000 people) • Excessive Tuberculation Identified Valve 112 24” Horizontal Gate • Valve Stem Compression Valve Installed in 1967 Failure REPAIR ACTIVITIES • Emergency Protocols Activated • 24/7 Repair Operations • Valve Replaced with Spool • 6 Days of 24-hr Operations • Repair Complete & System Pressure Restored - August 10th • Boil water Notice Lifted – August 12th CHALLENGES • Extreme Heat: 90- 96°F • Substructures Conflicts: Fiber Optics, Oil, and Gas Line • Shoring Modification • Deep Excavation INTERSYSTEM PUMPING SUPPORT • Deployed portable pumps to provide intersystem water supply to affected areas • Intersystem pumping between zones; lower pressure to higher pressure • Utilized MWD LA-25 connection to pump water via 3,000 feet of two 10-inch lay- flat hoses and high-capacity pumps to the intersection of Sesnon Blvd and Balboa Blvd PUBLIC NOTIFICATION • Notify LA • Wireless Emergency (WEA) • City EOC- Joint Information Center • Street Signs • LADWP.com website • ArcGIS Story Map • Social Media • Direct Customer Notification • 1-800 DIAL DWP • FAQs on Boil Water EMERGENCY PUBLIC WATER DISTRIBUTION • Coordinated 3 Bottled Water sites • 100+ Water employees staffing sites • Over 2M potable bottles distributed + recycled water COMMUNITY RESOURCES • Residential Delivery for Vulnerable Populations • Water Delivery for Equestrians • Water Provided to Schools • Portable Showers/ Restrooms • Portable Laundry INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENT • Increase Redundancy and Reliability • Two new 48-inch valves installed in February 2026 • One Overnight Installation Window NEXT STEPS TO MITIGATE FUTURE DISRUPTIONS • Water Infrastructure Plan • Large Valve Replacement Program Expansion • Portable Pump Testing Program • Provide Expanded Incident Command Training and Drills QUESTIONS? IMPACTED AREA
